# Heroes

> Heroes is a small compiled programming language designed so that every
> plausible LLM mistake is a compile error. Made for LLMs, yet plain to human
> eyes: no null, no exceptions, no implicit conversions, no standard library:
> everything comes from C through an FFI that clang verifies against the real
> headers. The compiler is written in Heroes and reproduces itself byte for
> byte: asked to compile itself it writes out the very C file the repository
> ships, and `cmp` finds nothing between them.

The entire language specification is deliberately small: it is measured
against a hard ceiling of 4096 tokens on every commit, because the spec is the
prompt and not documentation. If you are a language model asked to write
Heroes, read the spec first; it is the whole language:

- [The specification](https://heroes-lang.org/spec/): the whole language, under a 4096-token ceiling, written to be your prompt

**The repository is still private, so the two links under Source below answer
404 today.** Their addresses are final and open together with the code, once a
round of consolidation on the project is finished. Everything else here is on
this site and answers now: the specification above, every program under
`/examples/`, and the documentation under `/docs/`, which is the language
explained one idea at a time.

Ground rules a generated program must respect: exactly one way to write
anything (a canonical formatter; 4-space indentation, tabs are errors); named
arguments are mandatory where two parameters share a type; `match` is
exhaustive and `_` is forbidden on variants; failure is a value (`T?`,
`ok`/`fail`/`?`), there is no null and there are no exceptions; `???` is a
legal expression that reports what belongs in the gap instead of failing.

## Pages

- [Home](https://heroes-lang.org/): what the language is, one real sample, one real diagnostic, the claim
- [Examples](https://heroes-lang.org/examples/): every program in the repository, on the site, each with the exact command that runs it and the output it really prints. `/examples/index.json` is the same corpus as data, with a hash per file
- [Start](https://heroes-lang.org/start/): the four lines that build the compiler, where `heroes run` looks for the runtime, and the eleven verbs
- [Why Heroes](https://heroes-lang.org/why/): the founding constraint (no standard library), the thesis, the cost formula, the objections answered
- [The project](https://heroes-lang.org/project/): the fixpoint, over 180 modules and more than 55,000 lines of Heroes emitting byte-identical C; how a change to the language is decided by five judges; and the twenty lines `heroes this` prints
- [The author](https://heroes-lang.org/about/), and the credits at `/about/thanks/`: Giuseppe Arici, partner and CTO at Codermine in Brescia, author of *Heroes of code*, a history of programming languages framed as a dream journey with David Bowie as the guide, published on Amazon. He had never written a compiler before this one
- [Build log](https://heroes-lang.org/log/): one postcard per milestone, newest first
- [Thanks](https://heroes-lang.org/about/thanks/): the designers of every language Heroes borrowed from, named one by one, with what each borrowing was; links go to English Wikipedia only where an article about that person was verified to exist
- [Documentation](https://heroes-lang.org/docs/): the language page by page; every code block is a slice of a repository file that compiles and runs
- [Errors](https://heroes-lang.org/errors/): part of the documentation and linked from its landing page: diagnostics as a deliverable, real output with machine-applicable fixes tagged `certain`, and the per-mistake catch rates against a control build (a dropped argument label 76% vs 0%, a shadowed name 94% vs 0%, a lazy catch-all 100% vs 63%)

Every page above also exists in Italian under `/it/`, same filenames
(https://heroes-lang.org/it/ and so on), linked from each page's
`hreflang` alternates. The two editions are written independently rather than
machine-translated; code, compiler output and the twenty Zen lines are identical
in both, because they are quotations of real files and real output.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/heroes-lang/heroes): the compiler, the spec, the design record; build with `clang -I runtime seed/heroes.c runtime/runtime.c -o heroes`, then `./heroes run examples/gallery/00-first.hero`
- Every example is on the site rather than here: <https://heroes-lang.org/examples/>, cut from `examples/` when the site is built, in the canonical form `heroes fmt` prints

## Notes

- Status: written down as it happens, not packaged, and the repository is not
  public yet. The fixpoint is measured; the bootstrap compiler is archived and
  no longer builds; there is no installer, and the way in is a C compiler and
  one command.
- Diagnostics are machine-readable: `heroes check --json` emits schema 1 with
  stable snake_case codes, spans, notes and fixes.
